title: Ivo and the Ember Again
premise: Vesper Halloran, a mercenary sworn to the silent god Ember, has spent her life guarding the valley where magic cannot follow — until Ivo, a child speaking a language older than kingdoms, arrives at her door pursued by the king's inquisitors. The boy is not a child at all but the last ember of the god Vesper serves, reborn in mortal flesh, and both crown and church want him burned before he wakes. Torn between her oath to protect him and her duty to hand over what she was sworn to kill, Vesper flees the valley with Ivo, discovering that love outside the law is its own kind of faith. In the end, Vesper chooses to let the god die as a god so that Ivo can live as a boy, shattering her order's power and igniting a fragile new peace built on a lie she will carry forever.
about_author: Oscar Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about broken vows, quiet gods, and the people who keep loving them anyway.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She patrols the border stones of the Hollow Valley, where her mercenary order keeps magic out and the silent god Ember's memory alive. A routine day curdles when she finds a dead courier carrying an empty reliquary. Emotional beat: restless dread — something has changed beyond the stones.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On a rain-lashed night, a small boy appears at her cottage door, soaked, mute, and marked with a brand that matches her own oath-scar. He speaks one word in a language that predates kingdoms — and the ward-stones hum for the first time in centuries. Emotional beat: uncanny tenderness.

chapters.title: The Order of the Quiet Flame
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She brings Ivo to her chapter-house, where High Warden Corvane interrogates the boy and orders him confined. Vesper recognizes fear beneath the warden's piety. Emotional beat: first crack of doubt in the institution she gave her life to.

chapters.title: What the Boy Said
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, fragmentary and dreamlike. The boy remembers burning, falling, being many voices compressed into one small body. He does not know his own name; others named him. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief for a self he cannot locate.

chapters.title: Inquisitors at the Gate
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. King's inquisitors arrive demanding the 'anomalous child' be surrendered for trial by fire. Corvane agrees too quickly. Vesper watches Ivo flinch from flame during a 'blessing' and understands: they mean to burn him. Emotional beat: cold horror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Theft of a Small God
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She breaks her first oath in twenty years, stealing Ivo out through the catacombs beneath the chapter-house. Her sworn sister Maren catches her — and lets her go, at terrible cost. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of treason.

chapters.title: The Language Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the road, Ivo begins teaching Vesper fragments of his tongue; each word she learns unlocks a memory that isn't hers. She realizes the language is prayer — and that she is becoming fluent in someone else's soul. Emotional bond deepens into fierce maternal love.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Left behind, Maren covers Vesper's escape while cataloguing the order's hidden crimes: children taken, oaths bound with blood, a god deliberately silenced generations ago. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into quiet rebellion.

chapters.title: The Toll Bridge at Ashenford
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A checkpoint ambush forces Vesper to fight former comrades. She wins but spares them, and one — Sergeant Hale — sees her face clearly. Now the hunt is personal. Emotional beat: the cost of mercy made visible.

chapters.title: What Hunts Us
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The boy senses a pursuer that isn't human: the Hollow, an entity the order created to enforce the god's silence, feeding on spoken prayer. It is tracking Ivo's voice. Emotional beat: primal fear, and Ivo's first act of protection — going silent to shield Vesper.

chapters.title: The Witch of the Fen Road
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. They shelter with Sable, an exiled hedge-witch who recognizes what Ivo is and tells Vesper the truth: the boy is Ember's last ember, reborn. If he wakes fully, magic returns to the world — and the ancient war reignites. Emotional beat: the secret becomes unbearable weight.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The High Warden prays to a god he knows is dead, revealing in flashback that the order's founders murdered Ember to seize divine authority. He believes killing Ivo is mercy — for everyone else. Emotional beat: villainy rooted in sincere, poisoned faith.

chapters.title: Fire on the Mountain
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cornered in the passes, Vesper and Ivo are saved when Ivo involuntarily speaks — and the mountain answers. Magic leaks back into the world in ripples. Hale, witnessing it, defects to their side. Emotional beat: awe cracking open the old certainties.

chapters.title: The Choosing House
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They reach the ruined sanctuary where Ember died. Ivo's memories flood back fully through Vesper's learned prayers: he remembers his own murder, and remembers who wielded the knife — the first High Warden, Corvane's ancestor. Emotional beat: fury inherited across centuries.

chapters.title: What Vesper Swore
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashback chapter to the day of her oath: why a girl with nothing pledged herself to a silent god. Interwoven with present-day realization that her whole identity was built on a lie she helped enforce. Emotional beat: identity unmade.

chapters.title: The Hollow Finds Us
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The Hollow attacks at night, devouring sound itself. Ivo must speak to repel it — which will broadcast his location to every hunter in the kingdom. He speaks anyway, saving Vesper and Hale. Emotional beat: sacrifice as first true act of selfhood.

chapters.title: March of the Quiet Flame
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The order marches on the sanctuary with the inquisitors' army; Maren sabotages from within and is captured. Corvane offers Vesper absolution if she delivers the boy. Emotional beat: everything converges, no way back.

chapters.title: Trial by Fire
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the sanctuary, Ivo is seized and bound to the pyre where Ember died. Vesper stands before the assembled order and speaks the truth of the founding murder in the pre-kingdom tongue — and the words carry weight no human voice should have. Emotional beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: The God Who Wanted to Be a Boy
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. On the pyre, the ember within Ivo rises, offering to wake fully and return magic — at the price of the boy's self. Ivo refuses. He would rather be mortal, loved, and finite than eternal and alone. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — love against duty, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Emberfall
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Climax. Vesper cuts Ivo free as the ember gutters out; the god dies truly this time, and the Hollow unravels without a silence to enforce. Corvane, offered the dying god's last light, takes it and burns to ash rather than let the order survive on lies. Emotional beat: catharsis through loss.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Magic seeps gently back into the world; the order dissolves or reforms under Maren's leadership around service instead of silence. Vesper is offered sainthood and declines. Emotional beat: weary, hard-won peace.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Ember Again
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, years later. Ivo grows up ordinary in the valley, learning to fish and lie about chores. Vesper carries the secret of what she chose, and would choose it again. On the border stone, the boy asks her what the old word meant; she says: 'stay.' Emotional beat: quiet, earned grace.
